newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia financiers see 15 pct nominal peso fall.
newsitem.headline: Colombia financiers see 15 pct nominal peso fall.

text.p: Colombia's peso will devalue by 15 percent in nominal terms in calendar year 1997 and close at 1,160 against the dollar, the National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF) forecast Wednesday.

The central bank target is for a nominal devaluation of between 15 percent and 29 percent, amounting to a apreciation of between 3 percent and a devaluation of 11 percent once the inflation forecast of 18 percent is factored in.

ANIF chairman Armando Montenegro forecast Colombia would accumulate fresh net foreign reserves of about $1 billion this year compared with a government estimate of $750 million -- fueled by an influx of foreign investment and public and private sector debt.
Colombia's net foreign reserves stood at $10.3 billion as of July 4, the last date for which official figures are available.

Speaking at a forum on macroeconomic projections for 1997 and 1998, Montenegro said Colombia's on-going recession would drive down imports and greater restrictions would limit mean levels of foreign debt would grow by a modest 3.4 percent compared to 1996.
